text: >>1521117 >"An organized body of people with a particular purpose, a structure or arrangement of related or connected items." Antifa isn't organized at a collective level. Which is why it isn't an organization. Dipshit ESL. >they aren't aimless blobs that just accidentally trip on a banana peel at the same time and crash into another, and just so happen to decide "Hey let's set this dumpster on fire together at this particular street right now." There is degree of structure to make these things happen. And that structure is grassroots. This is like seeing pizza restaurants exist and concluding there is no way that many people could come up with putting tomato sauce and cheese on bread independent of one another, therefore all pizza restaurants must be part of an interconnected organization working together for some common goal. Instead of coming to the rational conclusion that tomato sauce and cheese on bread tastes good and are easy to prepare, and anyone with enough startup capital can sell that shit, therefore small groups of people can easily come to that line of work independently of one another. You can see how you're not being rational, right? I used pizza restaurants as an example, since conspiracies theories about those are more likely than not a safe space for you. Maybe remember what happened last time.
